description.narrative:
Project outcomes - Stakeholder effects: Increased access to finance for SMEs: Despite having a developed financial sector, SMEs in South Africa still experience challenges in accessing credit, mainly from insufficient collateral or guarantees required by the banks. By providing FRB additional funding dedicated to SME on-lending, the Project is expected to contribute to bridging this gap and increase access to finance for SMEs through an IFC existing client with a proven track-record in SME finance in the country. The Banks large branch network is a key asset to support access to finance for domestic SMEs.
Contribution to Market Creation - Competitiveness: The Project is part of a long-standing and multifaceted cooperation between IFC and FRB and marks the 5th investment project with the Bank targeting SME lending to increase access to finance for SMEs in South Africa. By supporting lending to SMEs in the country, the Project is expected to increase competitiveness among the domestic banks as many of them improve and scale up their SME product offerings.

The proposed investment consists of a senior unsecured loan of up to US$100 million to FirstRand Bank Limited (the Bank or FRB), an existing IFC client, under the MSME Finance Platform-SME Envelope for a maturity of up to 5 years. The Platforms SME Envelope seeks to address financial inclusion gaps, with a focus on reaching priority small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) segments, including women entrepreneurs, businesses in agriculture (Agri-SMEs), and supporting SME climate financing by providing medium- and long-term loans to eligible financial service providers. FirstRand Bank (FRB or the Bank) is a key strategic partner to IFC in South Africa, and the proposed project meets the IFC SME eligibility criteria for the country.
